newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee called $165 up, may stop at $75-$80.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee called $165 up, may stop at $75-$80.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE robusta coffee futures were due to open a sharp $165 higher on paper after another rally in New York on Wednesday but traders said the market could stop at $75 to $80.
On the charts, analysts said robustas were poised to scale much higher ground after Wednesday's winning streak which lifted the market out of its consolidation pattern.
"At the moment, it is very hard to say the market is not going forward," said Susan Rigg, an analyst at Chart Analysis. "If it is going to go up, it's going to go up."
London's July contract notched up some 7.6 percent gain on the day on Wednesday to settle at $2,258. This was the highest level since November 1995.
After London had closed, New York arabicas scored more gains to hit a new 20-year-peak at $2.97 a lb. It closed at 295.55 cents, still a hefty 21.25 cents up on the day.

Traders said the rally followed speculative buying on forecasts of cooler Brazilian weather. The last severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged more than half of Brazil's coffee trees.
Private U.S. forecaster Weather Serevices Corp said mostly fair and cool weather is forecast for Brazil's coffee belt on Thursday but no damaging cold was expected.
Temperatures were expected to be below normal with lows in the 40s to low 50s. The outlook for Saturday to Monday is similar.
Chart Analysis' Rigg said London's July could find a strong support at $2,100.
She said a break below $2,100 would certainly dent the current uptrend.
The 14-day relative strength indicator at 91 percent was well in the overbought territory of above 70-value barrier.
